XAVC-H (AKA AVCHD) is a niche, proprietary Sony codec that appears to be able to be accelerated by anything supporting AVC.

text: I am currently still using an EVGA RTX 2080 Super, paired with an AMD Ryzen 5 5600X and 16GB of 3600MHz CL17 RAM. At 2560x1440 resolution, there is one game I use DLSS on Quality setting, and that is Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy, because I am using the game's Ray Tracing features maxed out along with all the max graphics settings. Without DLSS the FPS would fluctuate between 45 and 60 with V-sync at 60Hz. With DLSS, I get a solid 60 FPS and I can only notice artifacts in the graphics if I really hunt for them. That said, I know I have the first generation of ray trace hardware, and Guardians of the Galaxy actually looks amazing with its ray tracing. I play one other game with full ray tracing (as limited as it is)  and that is Forza Horizon 5. In that game, I play with no DLSS or other upscale tricks, native 2560x1440, graphics settings all set to Ultra or High if that is the max, and get an average of 80 FPS locked to a solid 60Hz. Every other game I play either does not offer ray tracing or I do not have the horsepower to run ray tracing, so 99.5% of my gaming is rasterized. Cyberpunk 2077, native resolution, locked at 60Hz and it plays great. As long as games can maintain 60 FPS,  I am happy. That said, a large part of my game library plays at 120+ FPS at full resolution and often maxed out. All this is to be said, I want to upgrade graphics cards, but unless I get my hands on an AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D or Ryzen 9 5900X, I do not see a reason to "upgrade" to either the RTX 4060 or Intel B580. As a PC gamer on a budget, my PCs are always a mixture of new and used. Right now, nothing on the market offers a good enough value to me to upgrade from my current rig. I am happy enough with my current machine to still find the current generation of consoles to be, lacking, ray tracing is still not really a need for me though it would be nice to see performance increases there, and I am not a fan of what the upscale gimmicks like DLSS do to games that need to rely heavily on those gimmicks because the hardware can barely run the games. This is such a weird time in the PC industry. I know technologies evolve, ray tracing feels like a step in the right direction. But DLSS, FSR and XeSS feel like a step backwards in many ways, and feel like excuses for lazy code and terrible optimization. Sorry for the rant, just really tired of excuses and out right lies in everything in the real world these days.
